newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's GPE Industries to boost China drive.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's GPE Industries to boost China drive.

text.p: GPE Industries, a manufacturer of automotive electronic products, plans to make further inroads into China's car audio business through strategic alliances, company chairman Victor Lo said on Thursday.
"Now we will focus on China, but...we would like to do more in Asia outside China," Lo told reporters.
He said the company, which supplies 40 percent of China's car audio products, had seen a couple of strong years in sales and profit growth due to "good organic growth".
It intended to make further inroads into the world's most populous country through "selective mergers and acquisitions", he added.

Lo said that over the past 18 months, GPE Industries had forged strategic alliances with two Chinese firms -- First Auto Group in Changchun and Chongqing Changan Automotive Electronics -- and was negotiating a couple more joint ventures.
He declined to identify the potential new partners.
However, Lo said the company, a Singapore-listed unit of Hong Kong's Gold Peak Group, had to be "realistic" about its business strategy and expansion plans.
"We can't divert our resources now, away from audio and cabling. We have to be realistic with our resources," Lo said.
"Good targets are not easy to come by. We tend to be highly selective on our acquisitions," he said, adding that quality, a high level of technology and management strength were the criteria.
The company's two major businesses are automotive and home electronics, and cable and harness.

Lo said automative electronics provided 85 percent of the company's turnover of Singapore $176.5 million in the 1995/96 financial year that ended in March, and 15 percent came from the auto harness division. A wire harness is the nerve system connecting the electrical and electronic devices in a car.

However, he said there were no plans to expand into the cable and harness business in a big way, despite it being the faster growing sector, as the firm's strategy for now was to focus on automotive electronics.
Lo said China would remain a major production base for GPE Industries, although it planned to expand to other parts of Asia.
Lo said he was very bullish about China in the medium to long term as China now produced about 1.5-1.6 million vehicles of all types a year and was targeting 3.0 million by 2000.
"This means there is still lots of room...to produce automotive parts and components locally," Lo said, dismissing concerns of a slowdown in auto sales in China.

GPE Industries had its major plants in southern Guangdong province but planned to expand to other parts of China, Lo said. It produced about two million car radios annually, of which 600,000-700,000 were sold in China.
In the second quarter of this year, the company set up a research and development centre in Singapore, its first in Asia outside Hong Kong and China.
The company was listed on the Stock Exchange of Singapore in November 1995.
